summary: This program stores book titles in an ArrayList, prints them all, then reports how many there are, retrieves one by position, and shows that a list happily accepts the same title twice.

lines.text: ArrayList is the concrete, resizable list implementation that will actually hold the titles.
List is the interface that describes what a list can do, which lets the variable be declared in general terms.
The variable is typed as List but built as an ArrayList, so the rest of the code depends only on list behaviour; the <String> says every element must be a String.
add appends an element to the end of the list, and the list grows on its own to make room.
This enhanced for loop visits each element in order and copies it into title, which is simpler than tracking an index yourself.
size() reports how many elements the list currently holds, and the \n prints a blank line first to separate the sections of output.
get(0) retrieves the element at a position; list positions start at 0, so index 0 is the first book.
Adding a title that is already present succeeds, because a List allows duplicates and keeps items in insertion order.

lines.code: System.out.println("Total number of books after adding duplicate: " + bookTitles.size());
lines.text: Checking the size again proves the duplicate was stored as a separate fourth element rather than being ignored.
The two leading spaces and dash format each title as a bulleted item, making the final listing easy to read.
